narr: Several rounds of showers and thunderstorms occurred the weekend of July 12, influenced by remnant outflow boundaries, a stalled front, and a slow-moving upper low. A mesoscale convective vortex (MCV) further enhanced precipitation totals and rain rates, resulting in flash flooding primarily across Central Texas.
ev: Emergency management reported that Josey Lane between Keller Springs Road and Sherwood Lane in Carrollton was flooded by 1 foot of water, which was observed on the Josey flood gauge.
Emergency management reported that a high water rescue was conducted for a partially submerged vehicle near Addison Airport.
Emergency management reported that a water rescue was conducted for a stranded vehicle on the Interstate 35E frontage road north of Farmers Branch.
Emergency management reported that local first responders performed a high water rescue on HWY 183 between Lampasas and Lometa, where a car was swept off the road.
Emergency management reported that flooding covering US Highway 281 south of Adamsville resulted in a temporary closure of the highway.
McGregor Fire Department was dispatched to a swift water rescue at the South Bosque River crossing on Indian Trail just southeast of McGregor.
Emergency management reported that FM 933 was closed in both directions near County Road 1221 in Blum with a water rescue needed.
Emergency management reported that Highway 6 was closed in Iredell, and that most low water crossings across the north half of the county were closed due to flash flooding.
Emergency management reported that the 5700 block of FM 933 in Huron was down to 1 lane due to flash flooding.
Emergency management reported that the 1800 block along Highway 174 in Blum was closed due to high water.

Carrollton Police Department reported that the front of a westbound train was stuck in high water at the crossing at North Josey Lane and Sherwood Lane in Carrollton, which blocked Josey Lane. Traffic was backed up to Trinity Mills.
Broadcast media reported that flood waters covered Oakalla Road at the Clear Creek Bridge, between Oakalla and Maxdale, causing the road to be closed.
A public report indicated that multiple vehicles were stalled on Kelly Blvd near Creekview east of Carrollton due to high water. Kelly Blvd was shut down due to it being impassable.
